column2: My hands are in dough, three people text me at once, and I can't touch my phone. Other lenses help you cook. This one answers people while you cook.
Who wrote? Three names. I pick Mom.
Messy Hands Inbox. Look. Speak. Keep cooking.
First I planned it with the plan-lens interview. Where the card sits, how I act on it, and five checks it must pass.
Then Claude Code with Snap's CLAD agents built it in Lens Studio, over MCP. The agent pinches the buttons itself, takes a screenshot, and fixes what it sees.
Mom asks about Sunday. The card sits right of the dough, and never covers it.
Speak opens the draft. The gist in my words, and the clean reply under it, before anything goes.
Alex can wait. Remove. Two messages left.
Restart the Lens. It remembers what I answered and what I cleared.
What is real: the Lens, every button, memory, and twenty-three leef tests (LEAF). The messages and rewrites are sample data. Voice is off in this preview, so pinch does the same job.
The same moment from across the room. Left, what the glasses show. Right, the counter, the dough, and the card beside it.

Round two added memory and seventeen new leef tests (LEAF): empty inbox, taps in the wrong phase, reach, seated and standing, and a full demo tour. Three full runs in a row. Sixty-nine of sixty-nine pass.
This is one take, no cuts. Back to the list. Alex wants his keys.
